A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Finitely Presented Group|finitely presented]] [[Definition:Abelian Group|abelian group]] with relation matrix $\mathbf A \in \map {\MM_\Z} {n, m}$.
Then:
:$G \cong \Z^n / \Img {\mathbf A} \cong \displaystyle \bigoplus_{i \mathop = 1}^n \Z / d_i \Z$
where $d_i$ are the diagonal entries of the [[Definition:Smith Normal Form|Smith normal form]] of $\mathbf A$.

B_source.statement:
Let $f: A \to B$ be a [[Definition:Group Homomorphism|homomorphism]] of abelian groups.
Its [[Definition:Cokernel|cokernel]] is:
:$\operatorname {coker} f = B / \Img f$

substitutions.the map whose cokernel is taken: the relation matrix acting on the free abelian group
substitutions.the image being collapsed: the subgroup generated by the relations

derived.changing bases on source and target: row and column operations bringing the matrix to Smith normal form
derived.the cokernel of a diagonal matrix: the direct sum of cyclic groups given by the diagonal entries

validity_conditions: Invertible integer row and column operations amount to changes of basis on source and target, so they leave the cokernel unchanged up to isomorphism.
Every integer matrix can be brought to Smith normal form by such operations, since the integers form a principal ideal domain.
The cokernel of a diagonal matrix splits as a direct sum of cyclic groups, one per diagonal entry, with zero entries contributing free summands.
proof_plan:
Present $G$ as the [[Definition:Free Abelian Group|free abelian group]] $\Z^n$ on the generators modulo the image of $\mathbf A: \Z^m \to \Z^n$:
:$G \cong \operatorname {coker} \mathbf A$

For invertible $\mathbf P \in \map {\GL} {n, \Z}$ and $\mathbf Q \in \map {\GL} {m, \Z}$, $\mathbf P$ induces an [[Definition:Group Isomorphism|isomorphism]]:
:$\operatorname {coker} \mathbf A \cong \operatorname {coker} \paren {\mathbf P \mathbf A \mathbf Q}$

By [[Existence of Smith Normal Form]], choose $\mathbf P, \mathbf Q$ with $\mathbf P \mathbf A \mathbf Q = \operatorname {diag} \paren {d_1, \ldots, d_r, 0, \ldots}$ and $d_1 \divides d_2 \divides \cdots \divides d_r$.

The cokernel of a diagonal matrix is computed coordinatewise:
:$\operatorname {coker} \operatorname {diag} \paren {d_1, \ldots, d_n} = \displaystyle \bigoplus_{i \mathop = 1}^n \Z / d_i \Z$
with $\Z / 0 \Z = \Z$.
{{qed}}
